answer_summary: n = 10 carbon atoms. From the stated two-isotope carbon model, I[M]+/I[M+1]+ = p/(n·q) with p = 0.989 and q = 0.011, so the observed ratio 9 gives n = 989/99 ≈ 9.99, i.e. n = 10 (uniquely over the extraction table: n = 11 predicts 8.17 ≠ 9 at the printed precision). W carries a phenolic OH (Fe3+ colour change) and 10 carbons; among the table's candidates only compound 5 (C10H12O2, eugenol methyl ether, 4-allyl-1-methoxy-2-hydroxybenzene) satisfies both, so W = compound 5.
assumptions: Binomial (Bernoulli-product) isotope model: peak [M]+ = all-12C molecules, [M+1]+ = exactly-one-13C molecules (multiple 13C negligible); this model hierarchy is what the problem's assumptions stipulate, and the n-slot recurrence is proved in Lean.
13C abundance = 1 - 0.989 = 0.011, from the problem's exclusive-two-isotopes clause.
The printed ratio 9:1 is used exactly for solving; the integer fit is validated at half the unit quantum (IChO measurement policy).
Trusted general law (ordinary qualitative-analysis chemistry): a colour change with aqueous Fe3+ indicates a phenolic OH group; applied to the drawn extraction-table structures.
